purpose: Preserve and formalize the cross-surface visual language needed by Tablet /inventory and future surfaces without mutating canonical runtime authority in this candidate.

missingOrFragmentedAtCatalogLevel: semantic accent family covering cyan/gold/emerald/violet roles
cross-surface material language contract tying accents and glass behavior to recipes
explicit catalog entries for visual effect roles and their layer IDs
a governed ambient particle/sparkle capability; no canonical particle LayerId was found
explicit mapping between light-on/light-off presentation and the existing layer flag system
a single premium visual-language contract consumable by all surface adapters

glass.adaptationRule: Each surface adapter controls density, opacity, blur budget and composition. Do not copy Tablet shell geometry into PC/Mobile.

semanticAccents.cyan: information, active operational focus, selected/primary informational state
semanticAccents.gold: attention, commerce emphasis, cart/payment, premium highlight
semanticAccents.emerald: healthy, available, success, confirmed operational state
semanticAccents.violet: secondary analysis, structure, selected secondary emphasis

visualLanguage.accentRule: Accents are semantic and localized. They may appear in iconography, borders, glows, text highlights, selected states and radial illumination. They must not become a global page wash.

ambientParticles.policy: Do not invent or enable a production particle layer from this candidate. If required, create a separate governed capability proposal with performance/accessibility budget and exact layer ownership.

lightOn.meaning: premium effects profile enabled within the surface adapter budget
lightOn.mechanism: existing Layer Flags System/profile/explicit layer resolution

lightOff.meaning: effects suppressed for performance/accessibility or controlled comparison
lightOff.mechanism: existing Layer Flags System/profile/explicit layer resolution

shared-ui.character: neutral primitives consumed by surface adapters

requiredPromotionWork: Assign canonical neutral meaning for the semantic accent family without inventing NDC IDs.
Register/reconcile the shared visual-language catalog entries through the existing promotion mechanism.
Bind the shared accent/material/effect vocabulary to approved recipes and surface adapters.
Represent the existing layer IDs as governed visual effect capabilities rather than leaving them only in the UI-kit layer system.
Resolve whether a particle/sparkle effect is actually required; if yes, promote a bounded capability with evidence instead of inventing a layer.
Keep light-on/light-off as presentation state over the existing layer system, not as an uncontrolled duplicate theme mechanism.
Only after exact targets become APPLY_READY, update canonical RIFAT sources and deterministic projections.
Run cross-surface visual evidence so Tablet, PC and Mobile share language but remain adapted to their own interaction/density model.
explicitNonGoals: No runtime CSS mutation from this candidate.
No direct edit to generated projections.
No automatic conversion of every surface into Tablet Cloudglass.
No particle/WebGL effect without an explicit budget and promotion record.
